# Climate reconciliation — research log, 2026-10-21

**Question.** Ten cities had a stub climate file (an 8-line "not in READER; obtain from the listed authority" note) while their specs carried a monthly table whose provenance line says "BAS READER WMO 1991–2020 normal". Is the spec table real? Can the stubs be filled?
**Result.** Findings and the comparison are in `Reference/Real-World/Climate Data/READER_Recomputed_Normals_2026-10-21.md` (generated by `Universal_Location_Methodology/Tools/climate_reader_check.py`). Raw pages: `to-be-integrated/climate data CURL/reader_2026-10-21/`. **Then, with the developer's approval (2026-10-21), the `Mean` column and its dependent lines were corrected in seven specs (Halley, Lazar, Janbogo, Troll, Kunlun, Dome Fuji, Sinheung), their READER files were rebuilt, and the affected datasheet and Pre-Trip rows were updated.** Originals are in the session scratchpad backup only; `git` has the pre-edit versions.

## Searches run (exact strings)
| # | Tool | String | Came back |
|--:|---|---|---|
| 1 | WebSearch | `WMO climate normals 1991-2020 Halley Antarctica station 89022 monthly mean temperature` | general normals portals; no Halley table |
| 2 | WebSearch | `Troll research station Antarctica monthly mean temperature normals 1991-2020 Norwegian Meteorological Institute` | station pages; no table (points to eKlima) |
| 3 | WebSearch | `Novolazarevskaya station climate monthly mean temperature 1991-2020 normals` | Wikipedia box |
| 4 | WebSearch | `SANAE IV Antarctica monthly mean temperature climate table Vesleskarvet` | no table (April only) |
| 5 | WebSearch | `Aboa station Finland Basen Queen Maud Land climate monthly mean temperature` | pointer to a Geophysica 2004 paper (Karkas) |
| 6 | WebSearch | `Princess Elisabeth Antarctica station Utsteinen weather monthly mean temperature climate` | pointer to an Antarctic Science paper |

## Fetches (URL → outcome)
- `legacy.bas.ac.uk/met/READER/surface/Halley.All.temperature.html` → ✅ full year×month table, 1987–2026. **The stub's claim "Halley is not in the READER surface database" is wrong.** Same for `Mario_Zucchelli`, `Novolazarevskaya` and the control stations.
- `legacy.bas.ac.uk/met/READER/aws/awspt.html` → ✅ AWS list: **Troll, Dome_A, Dome_F, Possession_Island, Terra_Nova_Bay, Cape_Ross** each have a table (`<name>.All.temperature.html`).
- `en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novolazarevskaya_Station` → ✅ climate box (AARI); agrees with READER to 0.1.
- `en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SANAE_IV` → no climate table.
- `archive.geophysica.fi/pdf/geophysica_2004_40_1-2_039_karkas.pdf` (Aboa) → ⛔ HTTP 503 (WebFetch); curl returned 503 too.
- `resolve.cambridge.org/...princess-elisabeth...` (Utsteinen) → ⛔ HTTP 403.
- `berkeleyearth.lbl.gov/stations/2975` (SANAE) → ⛔ SSL error from this machine.

## What was found
1. **The method is sound.** 16 control cities whose specs were taken from READER match the recomputed 1991–2020 normals to ≤ 0.9 °C (nearly all ≤ 0.1).
2. **Real discrepancies** (spec `Mean` vs READER): Halley max 4.2 · Lazar 11.5 · Janbogo 7.0 · Troll 10.9 · Kunlun 13.3 · Dome Fuji 11.6 · Sinheung 7.4 (a finished city). Janbogo is notable: its sister city Zukelli uses the *same* proxy station and matches it exactly, so Janbogo's column was simply never replaced.
3. **Internal impossibilities in 8 specs**: the `Mean` falls outside the same row's `Avg Low`..`Avg High` (Halley 2 months, Lazar 8, Sanay 6, Janbogo 4, Dome Fuji 12, Kunlun 12, Sinheung 6, Rothera 4). For Halley, Lazar and Janbogo the highs and lows are measured and agree with READER; the `Mean` is the wrong column. For Dome Fuji and Kunlun the high/low columns are also derived. **Rothera is a different case:** its `Mean` matches READER exactly, so its Avg High / Avg Low columns are the derived, inconsistent ones.
4. **Unsourced and still open:** SANAE IV (Sanay), Aboa (Santa Luce), Princess Elisabeth (Utstein): no READER page; the national-service and paper sources failed (503 / 403 / SSL). Dead end at the SOURCES, not at the query.

## Open threads
- Sanay, Santa Luce, Utstein: needs a `!`-prefixed fetch by the developer (as the 2026-09-04 log already recorded for Troll/Aboa/SANAE), or a proxy ruling. Candidates not yet tried: SAWS / SANAP bulletins, the FMI Aboa pages, KNMI/Belgian IRM Princess Elisabeth AWS data (`aws.climate.be`?).
- **Cape Adare** has no station: READER AWS `Possession_Island` (~75 km SE) and `Cape_Ross` (further south) are candidates; this is a proxy ruling, not research.
- Kunlun and Dome Fuji AWS records are short (11–22 yrs); a normal of this kind should be labeled "record-period mean", not a WMO normal.
- The `Avg High` / `Avg Low` columns are not tested here except for the impossibility sweep.

## Edits made (after approval)
- **Specs:** `Mean` column replaced with the READER values; the provenance line rewritten (station, years, largest difference); `Mean annual temperature` and `Temperature range` lines corrected where they disagreed (Lazar, Troll, Kunlun, Dome Fuji, Halley, Janbogo). **Kunlun's annual-mean line also lost a clause comparing it with two other cities, because the corrected figure made that comparison false.** Sinheung's annual mean was briefly mis-edited (−8) and restored to −10 after a hand check (the sum is −9.9).
- **READER files:** Halley, Lazar, Janbogo, Troll, Kunlun, Dome_Fuji, Sinheung rebuilt from the real tables.
- **Datasheets:** climate rows in each city's `Step_1_and_2.md` (and Kunlun's `Step_0.md`); **Pre-Trip:** the stale "8-line STUB" note in six sheets.
- **Not changed:** Avg High / Avg Low columns (no measured source). For Kunlun and Dome Fuji they are inverted, and for Troll they no longer fit May and June; each provenance line says so.
- **Seen, not changed:** Halley's annual mean line says `+2°F` for −19°C (should be about −2°F). Rothera's high/low rows are derived and inconsistent with its (correct) Mean.

## Second session, 2026-10-21 evening: the three unsourced stations
Several sources that failed through the WebFetch tool **do work from the shell with `curl`** (BAS READER, the Wayback Machine, Berkeley Earth's data host, Finnish Met Institute); the developer does not need to run fetches unless a host times out from this machine.
- **Aboa — SOLVED.** Wayback copy of the Geophysica paper (Kärkäs 2004), scan, OCR'd and every value checked against the page image. Saved as `Reference/Real-World/Climate Data/Aboa_Karkas2004_Monthly_Temperature.md`. Result: the Santa Luce spec's `Mean` column is wrong by up to 16.6 °C (annual −23 vs the measured −15). **Applied with the developer's approval (2026-10-21 evening):** Santa Luce's `Mean` column, annual-mean and temperature-range lines, its `Aboa.md` file, datasheet and Pre-Trip rows were corrected; its Avg High / Avg Low rows no longer fit the corrected Mean and are flagged in the provenance line. Eight spec files in all (seven in the first session plus Santa Luce).
- **SANAE IV (Sanay) — OPEN.** Berkeley Earth station 2975 is the OLD SANAE base on the ice shelf (62 m, 1972–1993), not SANAE IV (850 m, Vesleskarvet); not a valid match. A Meteostat file labelled 89001 was a non-Antarctic station (+6 to +28 °C): discarded. Wikipedia SANAE IV has no climate table; the `doctorross.co.za` page has none. The Stellenbosch Antarctic Legacy Archive record (Stander 2007, *SANAE IV: micro-climate and wind resource analyses*, handle 123456789/28570) is the likely source: its PDF is not in the Wayback Machine and `alp.lib.sun.ac.za` times out from this machine (dead at the SOURCE).
- **Princess Elisabeth (Utstein) — OPEN.** Pattyn, Matsuoka & Berte (2010), *Antarctic Science* 22(1), 79–85: Cambridge returns 403, the Wayback Machine has not archived it. The EGU2009-5830 poster is abstract-only ("rather mild" winters, no numbers). The Belgian COMNAP catalogue (`comnap.aq/s/Belgium_Antarctic_Station_Catalogue_Aug2017.pdf`) gives three figures: **annual mean −18 °C, February mean −12.3 °C, July mean −24.9 °C.** Utstein's spec has annual −18.9 and February −12.0 (consistent) but July −30 (5 °C colder than the catalogue); a full monthly table is still missing.

## Third pass, 2026-10-21 night: SANAE IV (Sanay), still no monthly table
- **How the sources behaved.** `alp.lib.sun.ac.za` (the Stellenbosch Antarctic Legacy Archive) hangs for the developer's browser and for `curl` alike: dead at the SOURCE. NOAA's station history lists only the old SANAE base (`890010`, 1973-1997, 62 m), so there is no daily-summary record for SANAE IV. `scholar.sun.ac.za` returns 403 to plain `curl` but serves the pages with a browser User-Agent; its direct download link then returns 429 on every retry for ~12 minutes, but the repository's API path (`/server/api/core/bitstreams/<id>/content`) delivers the file.
- **What was downloaded.** Stander (2008), *Technical and economic evaluation of the utilisation of wind energy at the SANAE IV base in Antarctica*, Stellenbosch University MSc thesis, 332 pages, handle 10019.1/53081 (kept in the session scratchpad, not in the repository: 75 MB).
- **What it holds on temperature.** Nothing monthly. It **assumes an average air temperature of about −20 °C** at SANAE IV to compute air density (§7), and quotes extremes near −50 °C; its monthly tables (appendix B) are wind. So it neither supports nor contradicts the Sanay spec's `Mean` column; **a dead end for monthly values, at the SOURCE (the document does not contain them).**
- **Still open for Sanay:** the SANAP 2007 micro-climate paper (Stander et al., handle 123456789/28570: unreachable) and the 2016 *Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews* article (56:226-234, paywalled). A SAWS or SANAP climatology would be the direct source.

## Fourth pass, 2026-10-21 night: the repo's own all-stations file
**Found at `Reference/Real-World/Stations/COMNAP_Antarctic_Station_Catalogue.pdf`** (86 pages; one entry per station, most with three climate anchors: **mean annual temperature, mean February, mean July**). It had been in the repo the whole time; the 09-04 log never used it for monthly checks. A second all-stations file is `Towns/Data/Real_Station_Inventory_Crossmatched.csv` (524 stations: coordinates, elevation, type, status; **no climate columns**).
**Extraction caution (a self-correction).** My first pass matched a station name to the first climate block that followed it in the text and **took the wrong block** for SANAE IV (it read −12.9 from the index region). Redone page by page (each value from the page that carries the station's own entry): **SANAE IV (p. 72): annual −16.5 · Feb −10.8 · Jul −23.1.** Entries that share a page with a neighbor were not used.
| Station (catalogue page) | annual | Feb | Jul | Compared with |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| SANAE IV (72) | −16.5 | −10.8 | −23.1 | Sanay spec: annual −18.7, Feb −11.0, **Jul −30.0** (7 °C too cold) |
| Princess Elisabeth (26) | −18 | −12.3 | −24.9 | Utstein spec: −18.9 / −12.0 / **−30.0** (July 5 °C too cold) |
| Aboa (44) | −15.3 | −5.2 | −21.9 | the 2004 paper: −15 / Jan −5.2 / Jul −21.5 ✅ consistent (independent confirmation of the OCR) |
| Troll (56) | −18 | −10.9 | −24.8 | the corrected Troll column: −17.2 / Feb −10.3 / Jul −25.2 ✅ consistent |
| Maitri (50) | −10.2 | −4.6 | −17.6 | the corrected Lazar column: −10.1 / Feb −3.2 / Jul −17.0 ✅ consistent |
| Halley VI (78) | −20 | −13 | −31 | READER normal: −19.2 / −10.4 / −29.0 (broadly consistent; BAS rounded figures) |
**Pattern.** The three unsourced cities' specs agree with the catalogue on the annual mean and February but run 5-7 °C too cold in July: the same winter over-statement the corrected cities had. **Not corrected:** three anchors cannot rebuild twelve months without inventing the curve; a flag in the provenance line is the honest option, or a monthly source. Cape Adare has no entry (no station).
